system.summary: Two-part (randomised) Portuguese telegraph code of five-figure groups with words, phrases, syllables and endings, and two-figure punctuation groups (06 full stop, 04 comma).
system.sibling_key: Not the code of carlos1903, sabugosa1910, manuel1910 or hintze1903: no group shared (groups.py, part 5).
system.notes: distinct_symbols and nomenclator.entries = the 261 groups with a value from the glosses (code_values.tsv), not the size of the code; two-figure items 04 and 06 included. Order test: Spearman rho 0.068 between group number and alphabetical order over 227 cleanly glossed groups; 30% of 2000 shuffles reach it. unread_groups = the nine items flagged x in groups.py.

prior_solution.where: The receiver's pencil decode above the groups on every coded form of M09. No printed decipherment found in one web search.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT chose the catalogue items and set the rules; AI language-model agents fetched the images, transcribed the strips and glosses, paired them, ran the controls, and reviewed the readings against the scans. No hand correction of readings recorded.
tools: groups.py (groups with glosses, transcription cross-check, word-count control, order test with shuffle control, comparison with the sibling codes)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT); a vision-capable language model for the transcription

solution.what: All 21 images of M09 fetched through the DigitArq JSON backend; 9 telegrams on 11 forms, the even images mostly backs.
Transcribed the eight coded telegrams (409 code items) with the pencil gloss over each group, and the clear telegram m0003-m0004.
Paired each group with the receiver's gloss: 261 values; recurring groups agree up to inflection (teve/tem, terá/teria) except 43243 in m0011.

Taxed word count: code items + clear words + 9 address words equal the header on m0005, m0007, m0011, m0014; m0020 equals the receiver's pencilled 83; m0009 and m0018 are one short (m0009 with the office's note of a missing word).
Rank correlation of group number with the alphabetical order of the value: rho 0.068, inside the shuffle null; the code is two-part, so open groups cannot be bracketed.

A reviewing agent re-read six telegrams against the full-resolution scans and corrected five readings: m0011 opens "Em combinação com o Porto e Serpa" (not "Em Coimbra, como"), 93186 G.C. Legião, 69958+66931 tend-es, 51443 contar com and 19864 isso, 48696 Hen[daya?]; 43243 in m0011 left open.
Built the readings with the corrections; 10231 + 01021 glossed medi + na read as Medi-na in both places of m0011. 400 of 409 items read.

Compared the 261 groups with the codes of carlos1903, sabugosa1910, manuel1910 and hintze1903: no group shared, where the ten commonest groups of this code would be expected (P(none) below 2e-6 each). A different code.
One web search (Venceslau de Lima, telegrams to Manuel II, 1909 journey, Medina, Bussaco): biographies only, nothing on these telegrams. Editions of Manuel II's papers not searched.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent decoder (verify_dudout_20261114.py) reading only code_values.tsv and the eight m*_transcription.txt: 409 code items, same groups in the same order as the m*_decryption.txt files, 409/409 values equal to the published glosses. Read bar recounted: the recorded read_share is items glossed / items (e.g. m0011 97/101); v10_relabel on m*_reading.md gives 0.868-0.973 because it counts 31 editorial supplements ([o], [a], [da], [Lima], Pres[idente da], G[rã-]C[ruz da] [de Honra]) and doubt marks written [?] after glossed words as holes. With the supplements not counted: m0001 1.0, m0005 1.0, m0007 0.991, m0009 0.970, m0011 0.937, m0014 1.0, m0018 0.981, m0020 0.963; m0011 alone stays under 0.95 (4 open groups and Hen[daya?]). Class left to the maintainer; images not re-read.

outcome.method_basis: Every coded telegram carries the receiver's pencil decode above its groups; the readings follow it, with five corrections from a review against the scans; 261 code values were then tabulated by pairing groups with the glosses (an extension of the decipherment of the time, not cryptanalysis).

parts.label: The eight coded telegrams (decodes above the groups)
parts.basis: One rule for all eight: a telegram is read when at least 95% of its words read as sense. Each is at 95.7% or above; 9 of 409 code items stay open (no-key-material or illegible), and faint glosses leave one clause unclear in m0009, m0011 and m0020.

parts.label: Lima's two-part code, 261 values
parts.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
parts.basis: Groups paired with the interlinear glosses; repeated groups agree.

outcome.fraction_read_source: groups_output.txt part 3: code items (documents[].length) with a gloss that enters the reading; the nine items flagged x in groups.py are unread: 400 / 409 = 0.978.

texts.label: m0001, Lisbon -> Madrid (Palacio Real), 12 Nov 1909
texts.summary: At the start of the King's state visit, Lima repeats his congratulations on the welcome in Madrid; coded: all continues without news, he is writing to Windsor.

reading_review.note: Clean Portuguese; only four groups coded, the rest in clear.

texts.label: m0005, Lisbon -> Paris, 30 Nov 1909
texts.summary: Confidential: a stop at Bussaco would be awkward, so the King should come straight by the night express; Vasconcellos Porto presses for an answer.

reading_review.note: Coherent; a few articles supplied in brackets and the signature's last word supplied.

texts.label: m0007, Lisbon -> Paris, 2 Dec 1909
texts.summary: The return journey settled: arrival in Lisbon at 1.15 pm, greetings at Vilar Formoso, rest as far as Pampilhosa, lunch between Santarém and Lisbon.

reading_review.note: Long, coherent railway-timetable telegram; one hour figure unread.

texts.label: m0009, Lisbon -> Paris, 30 Nov 1909
texts.summary: No answer yet to Saturday's telegram about the return trains; the departure is the day after tomorrow and nothing is fixed; Lima asks for a decision most urgently.

reading_review.note: Coherent; two groups unread after 'tem telegraphado', otherwise clean.

texts.label: m0011, Lisbon -> Paris, 27 Nov 1909
texts.summary: Lima proposes the return route: the 7.40 pm night train from Paris to Medina del Campo and a special train to Lisbon, cutting out the stop at Luso.

reading_review.note: Coherent overall; about five groups unread or doubtful in the train arrangements (the Hendaye passage).

texts.label: m0014, Lisbon -> Paris, 28 Nov 1909
texts.summary: Since the French President has given the Grand Cross of the Legion of Honour to Bocage, the King should be friendly to Briand, with no inequality against England and Spain.

reading_review.note: Coherent; the abbreviated title (G. C. Legião) expanded in brackets.

texts.label: m0018, Lisbon -> Paris, 28 Nov 1909
texts.summary: Lima edits the King's reply toast for the President's dinner, adding friendship, thanks for the welcome in "intellectual Paris" and the tightening of relations.

reading_review.note: Coherent and clean; the toast amendments read word for word, one group doubtful.

texts.label: m0020, Lisbon -> Paris, 30 Nov 1909
texts.summary: Confidential: the King should go only to São Carlos on the night of his arrival and hold the reception at the station; Lima asks for an answer.

reading_review.note: Coherent except one clause ('[?] me disse se inconveniencia ...') whose sense is not clear; the translation says so.

outcome.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (catalogue 409). The catalogue entry counts ten telegrams and places them in the 1909 cabinet crisis; the unit holds nine telegrams of the King's state visit and return journey, Nov-Dec 1909, eight with code, all with the receiver's pencil decode. The clear telegram of 9 Nov (m0003-m0004) is in related_clear.md.
